questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman presents to the clinic with a 3-month history of a persistent cough, unintentional weight loss, and night sweats. A chest X-ray reveals findings consistent with pulmonary tuberculosis. After confirming the diagnosis, the physician prescribes a multi-drug therapy (MDT) regimen. What is the most important reason for using MDT in her treatment?

options.label: A
options.text: To enhance the speed of clinical recovery

options.label: B
options.text: To reduce the duration of treatment

options.label: C
options.text: To prevent the emergence of drug-resistant strains

options.label: D
options.text: To reduce the adverse side effects of anti-tubercular drugs

questions.answerText: To prevent the emergence of drug-resistant strains
questions.solutionHtml:
n>

A. To enhance the speed of clinical recovery

While MDT can help in effective treatment and clinical recovery, this is not the primary reason for its use. The main goal is to prevent drug resistance.

B. To reduce the duration of treatment

Although MDT can help to reduce the overall duration of treatment compared to monotherapy, this is not the primary reason for its use. The main objective remains the prevention of drug-resistant TB strains.

D. To reduce the adverse side effects of anti-tubercular drugs

Each anti-tubercular drug can have side effects. By using multiple drugs, it's possible to give each drug at a lower dose than if used alone, potentially reducing the severity of side effects. However, this is not the primary reason for using MDT. The main rationale behind MDT is the prevention of drug resistance, not the minimization of side effects.

Educational Objective

Multi-drug therapy (MDT) is crucial in the treatment of tuberculosis to prevent the emergence of drug-resistant strains of Mycobacterium tuberculosis. While MDT can also reduce the overall treatment duration, its primary purpose is to ensure that the bacteria are effectively eradicated by using a combination of drugs, thereby minimizing the risk of developing resistance to any single drug.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man presents to the clinic with recurrent oral herpes outbreaks. He mentions that his outbreaks were previously well controlled with acyclovir, but recently, the medication seems less effective. The physician suspects the herpes simplex virus (HSV) causing his symptoms might have developed resistance to acyclovir. Resistance to acyclovir is most commonly due to mutation in a viral gene that encodes a protein that:

options.label: D
options.text: Transports acyclovir out of the cell

questions.solutionHtml:
/span>

This description matches the function of reverse transcriptase, which is not relevant to the herpes simplex virus (HSV) as HSV is a DNA virus, not an RNA virus.

B. Transports acyclovir into the cell

The transport of acyclovir into the cell is not the primary mechanism of resistance. Acyclovir enters the cell via diffusion and not through a specific transport protein.

D. Transports acyclovir out of the cell

There is no significant evidence that resistance to acyclovir is due to the transport of the drug out of the cell.

Educational Objective

Resistance to acyclovir in herpes simplex virus (HSV) is primarily due to mutations in the viral thymidine kinase gene. Thymidine kinase is crucial for the initial phosphorylation of acyclovir to its active form. Mutations in this enzyme reduce the ability of the virus to phosphorylate acyclovir, leading to decreased drug efficacy.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old male diagnosed with HIV seeks guidance from his primary care doctor for appropriate treatment. Given the significant drop in his CD4 counts, initiation of HAART (Highly Active Antiretroviral Therapy) is being contemplated. Concerning the role of ritonavir for this patient, which statement holds true?

options.label: A
options.text: Ritonavir is commonly used to inhibit the HIV protease enzyme along with other drugs in HAART regimen.

options.label: B
options.text: This agent is associated with resistance when used in combination with another protease inhibitor.

options.label: C
options.text: It is used primarily for its inhibitory effect on CYP3A4.

options.label: D
options.text: This is an excellent single agent for use in HAART therapy.

questions.answerText: It is used primarily for its inhibitory effect on CYP3A4.
questions.solutionHtml:
/span>

A. Ritonavir is commonly used to inhibit the HIV protease enzyme along with other drugs in HAART regimen.

While ritonavir does have protease inhibitory activity, its primary role in HAART regimens is as a pharmacokinetic enhancer of other protease inhibitors rather than as the main protease inhibitor.

B. This agent is associated with resistance when used in combination with another protease inhibitor.

Ritonavir, when used in low doses as a booster, does not contribute significantly to resistance. Its role is to increase the effectiveness of other protease inhibitors without leading to increased resistance.

D. This is an excellent single agent for use in HAART therapy.

Ritonavir is not used as a single agent in HAART therapy due to its side effect profile and the development of resistance when used alone. It is always used in combination with other antiretroviral drugs.

Educational Objective

Ritonavir is primarily used in HAART regimens for its strong inhibitory effect on the cytochrome P450 enzyme CYP3A4. This inhibition enhances the pharmacokinetics of other protease inhibitors, increasing their plasma levels and efficacy, which allows for lower dosages and reduced side effects.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old female discovered she was HIV-positive four weeks ago. Upon receiving her diagnosis, she initiated a HAART (Highly Active Antiretroviral Therapy) protocol. Currently, she's experiencing symptoms of nausea, episodes of vomiting, and stomach pain. Lab tests indicate a heightened serum amylase level. If these symptoms are a result of her medication, which antiretroviral drug is most likely the culprit?
questions.solutionHtml:
strong>

A. Efavirenz

Efavirenz is a non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI) that is more commonly associated with central nervous system side effects such as dizziness, insomnia, and vivid dreams rather than gastrointestinal side effects and pancreatitis.

C. Raltegravir

Raltegravir is an integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI) and is not typically associated with pancreatitis. Its common side effects include elevated creatine kinase, muscle pain, and insomnia.

D. Nevirapine

Nevirapine is another NNRTI that is primarily associated with hepatotoxicity and skin rash, including severe reactions like Stevens-Johnson syndrome, rather than pancreatitis.

Educational Objective

Didanosine, an NRTI used in HAART regimens, is associated with gastrointestinal side effects, including pancreatitis. Elevated serum amylase levels, along with symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, and stomach pain, are indicative of pancreatitis.

questions.stem: A 7-year-old girl comes to the medical office complaining of a severely pruritic skin condition that started 3 days ago. Three other children from her school have been diagnosed with similar skin complaints. On examination, the girl has itchy red bumps and clear linear tracks, particularly on her finger webs of hand and feet and on ankles. They somewhat resemble the marks left by tiny insects. What would be the best course of action for treating this condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Topical permethrin.

 

The clinical presentation given — itchy red bumps and clear linear tracks, especially on the feet, ankles, and behind the knees — is indicative of scabies. Scabies is a skin infestation caused by the Sarcoptes scabiei mite.

 

  • Topical agents like miconazole: Miconazole is an antifungal agent and is primarily used for fungal infections like athlete's foot or ringworm. Scabies is caused by a mite, not a fungus, so miconazole would not be effective for this condition.
  • Oral ivermectin: Ivermectin can be effective against scabies, especially in cases where the standard topical treatment fails or for severe forms such as crusted scabies. However, it is not typically the first-line treatment for common scabies.
  • Topical permethrin: This is the correct choice. Permethrin cream is the first-line treatment for scabies. It is applied to the entire body from the neck down and left on for 8-14 hours, usually overnight. The treatment kills the mites and their eggs. It's crucial that family members and other close contacts be treated simultaneously to prevent re-infestation, even if they are asymptomatic.
  • Skin creams containing steroids: While steroid creams can reduce inflammation and itching, they do not address the underlying cause, which is the mite infestation. Using steroids alone would not eradicate the mites and could even make the condition worse.

questions.stem: A 57-year-old male patient with a history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension is admitted with a 7-day history of fever, cough, and increasing shortness of breath. A PCR test confirms a diagnosis of COVID-19. Chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral infiltrates indicative of pneumonia, and his oxygen saturation on room air registers at 88%. Considering the current understanding of COVID-19 treatments, which therapeutic approach is most suitable to enhance this patient's clinical outcome?

options.label: B
options.text: Combination of high-flow oxygen and dexamethasone therapy.

options.label: D
options.text: Treatment with monoclonal antibodies against SARS-CoV-2.

questions.answerText: Combination of high-flow oxygen and dexamethasone therapy.
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Combination of high-flow oxygen and dexamethasone therapy.

 

  • Administration of remdesivir: Remdesivir, an antiviral drug, has been shown to shorten the duration of symptoms in certain hospitalized COVID-19 patients, but its effect on mortality is less clear. It might be considered, especially in the earlier course of severe disease, but its benefit in terms of clinical outcomes isn't as well-established as dexamethasone in hypoxic patients.
  • High-flow oxygen and dexamethasone therapy: Hypoxemic patients with COVID-19 benefit from oxygen supplementation. Dexamethasone has shown mortality benefits in hypoxic COVID-19 patients, making it the recommended therapeutic approach for those with significant respiratory compromise, like in this presented case.
  • Intravenous administration of tocilizumab: Tocilizumab, an IL-6 receptor antagonist, is used to treat cytokine release syndrome, which can be a complication of severe COVID-19. While it can be beneficial for select hospitalized patients, its specific role in therapy isn't as clearly defined as dexamethasone for those with significant hypoxemia.
  • Treatment with monoclonal antibodies against SARS-CoV-2: Monoclonal antibodies targeting SARS-CoV-2, such as bamlanivimab or casirivimab-imdevimab combo, have been authorized for use in certain non-hospitalized patients with mild to moderate symptoms and are at high risk for progressing to severe disease. They are less commonly used in severe hospitalized cases, like the patient described here.

questions.stem: Which of the following anti-tubercular drugs is safe in hepatitis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Streptomycin

 

  • Isoniazid:
    Isoniazid is hepatotoxic and is one of the medications most commonly associated with drug-induced hepatitis. It is not considered safe in patients with preexisting liver disease such as hepatitis.
  • Rifampicin:
    Rifampicin is another drug that has hepatotoxic potential. It can induce liver enzymes and, in some cases, can cause hepatocellular damage, especially when used in combination with other hepatotoxic drugs.
  • Ethionamide:
    Ethionamide can also cause hepatic toxicity, including hepatitis. It is not recommended for use in patients with liver disease.
  • Streptomycin:
    Streptomycin is primarily nephrotoxic and ototoxic but is not associated with hepatotoxicity, making it a safer option in patients with liver disease like hepatitis. Therefore, it is considered safe in hepatitis compared to the other options listed.

questions.stem: A patient presents with a single hypoesthetic patch on the skin, suggestive of paucibacillary leprosy. According to current guidelines, what is the treatment of choice for this patient?

options.label: A
options.text: Rifampicin + Ofloxacin + Minocycline as a single dose

options.label: B
options.text: Rifampicin + Clofazimine + Dapsone for one year

options.label: C
options.text: Rifampicin + Dapsone + Clofazimine for six months

questions.answerText: Rifampicin + Dapsone + Clofazimine for six months
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Rifampicin + Dapsone + Clofazimine for six months

 

  • Rifampicin + Ofloxacin + Minocycline as a single dose:
    While this regimen might have been used for single-lesion PB leprosy in the past, it is no longer the standard treatment according to updated guidelines that recommend a three-drug regimen for all types of PB leprosy.
  • Rifampicin + Clofazimine + Dapsone for one year:
    This regimen is typically for multibacillary (MB) leprosy and involves a longer duration of treatment than is generally necessary for PB leprosy.
  • Rifampicin + Dapsone + Clofazimine for six months:
    According to updated guidelines, this is now the treatment of choice for paucibacillary leprosy.
  • Rifampicin + Dapsone for 6 months:
    This was the previous standard treatment for PB leprosy but has been updated to include Clofazimine for a three-drug regimen.Top of Form

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman presents to the clinic with symptoms of fever, weight loss, and splenomegaly. She has recently returned from a trip to a region known for endemic visceral leishmaniasis, also known as Kala-azar. Which of the following medications is suitable for single-dose treatment of Kala-azar?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Liposomal Amphotericin B

 

Liposomal Amphotericin B is the preferred drug for Kala-azar and has been successfully used in single-dose regimens. Its efficacy and safety profile make it suitable for single-dose treatment.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Pentamidine: Although Pentamidine can be used for the treatment of Kala-azar, it is not suitable for single-dose treatment and has significant side effects.

 

Option C. Sodium stibogluconate: Sodium stibogluconate requires a more extended course of treatment and is not suitable for single-dose treatment.

 

Option D. Miltefosine: Miltefosine is an oral medication and requires a more extended course of treatment, making it unsuitable for single-dose treatment.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman presents to the clinic for a routine check-up. Blood tests reveal elevated liver enzymes, and subsequent tests confirm a diagnosis of chronic hepatitis C. She has no significant medical history and wishes to begin antiviral therapy to minimize the risk of progression to liver cirrhosis or hepatocellular carcinoma. Which of the following oral medications is recommended as a first-line treatment for hepatitis C?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Sofosbuvir

 

  • Ribavirin:
    Ribavirin is an older antiviral medication that was used in combination with interferon for treating hepatitis C. It is not commonly used as a monotherapy for hepatitis C and has largely been replaced by more effective and tolerable options.
  • Tenofovir:
    Tenofovir is primarily used in the treatment of HIV and chronic hepatitis B, not hepatitis C.
  • Sofosbuvir:
    Sofosbuvir is a first-line, direct-acting antiviral agent used for the treatment of chronic hepatitis C. It is often used in combination with other medications and has a high cure rate with a well-tolerated side effect profile.
  • Lamivudine:
    Lamivudine is used for the treatment of hepatitis B and HIV but is not effective for treating hepatitis C.

questions.stem: Which of the following combination of drug and its indication is FALSE?

options.label: C
options.text: Tafenoquine: Single dose treatment of P. falciparum malaria

options.label: D
options.text: Remdesivir: Moderate to severe COVID-19 pneumonia

questions.answerText: Tafenoquine: Single dose treatment of P. falciparum malaria
questions.solutionHtml:
span>

Explanation of Other Options

A. Pretomanid: MDR tuberculosis

This statement is correct. Pretomanid is used in combination with other drugs for the treatment of multi-drug resistant (MDR) tuberculosis.

B. Fostemsavir: Treatment of HIV

This statement is correct. Fostemsavir is an antiretroviral medication used in the treatment of HIV infection.

D. Remdesivir: Moderate to severe COVID-19 pneumonia

This statement is correct. Remdesivir is an antiviral drug that has been used for the treatment of moderate to severe COVID-19 pneumonia.

Educational Objective

Understanding the specific indications for various drugs is crucial for their appropriate use. Pretomanid is used for MDR tuberculosis, fostemsavir for HIV treatment, and remdesivir for moderate to severe COVID-19 pneumonia. Tafenoquine, however, is primarily indicated for the radical cure of P. vivax malaria and not as a single-dose treatment for P. falciparum malaria.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about fluconazole is most accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: It is the drug of choice for the treatment of aspergillosis

options.label: B
options.text: It does not penetrate the blood-brain barrier

options.label: C
options.text: Its oral bioavailability is less than that of ketoconazole

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. It inhibits demethylation of lanosterol

    •  
  • It is the drug of choice for the treatment of aspergillosis:
  • This statement is incorrect. Voriconazole and Amphotericin B are more commonly used as the first-line agents for the treatment of invasive aspergillosis. Fluconazole is primarily used for candidiasis and cryptococcal meningitis.
  • It does not penetrate the blood-brain barrier:
  • This statement is incorrect. Fluconazole is well known for its ability to penetrate the blood-brain barrier. This characteristic makes it an effective choice for fungal infections of the central nervous system, such as cryptococcal meningitis.
  • Its oral bioavailability is less than that of ketoconazole:
  • This statement is incorrect. Fluconazole has a high oral bioavailability, which is one of its advantages. When taken orally, it is well absorbed, and its bioavailability is not significantly affected by food intake. Ketoconazole's bioavailability can be affected by factors like stomach acid levels and food.
  • It inhibits demethylation of lanosterol:
  • This statement is correct. Fluconazole, like other azole antifungals, works by inhibiting the enzyme lanosterol 14α-demethylase (often abbreviated as CYP51). This enzyme is involved in the conversion (demethylation) of lanosterol to ergosterol. Ergosterol is an essential component of the fungal cell membrane, and its deficiency leads to cell membrane disruption and fungal cell death.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old Indian man, pursuing his post-graduation, recently returned from Africa where he completed an academic research project. A few weeks after his return, he visits the hospital after testing positive for Plasmodium vivax malaria. The doctor recommends primaquine for the radical cure of his P. vivax infection. Shortly after beginning the regimen, the patient exhibits yellowing of the eyes. What could be the most probable reason for this symptom?

options.label: A
options.text: Primaquine merely stains the tears yellow; this isn't genuine yellowing of the eyes.

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Deficiency of a specific enzyme.

 

The presented situation suggests a reaction attributable to G6PD (Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase) deficiency. People from certain ethnic groups, including some Indians, are more likely to have this enzyme deficiency. When patients with G6PD deficiency are exposed to specific medications, such as primaquine, they can experience hemolysis (breakdown of red blood cells). This hemolysis can result in jaundice, leading to the yellowing of the eyes.

  • While some medications can cause a discoloration of the tears, primaquine doesn’t typically lead to yellow tears that would be mistaken for jaundice.

  • Without additional details on other medications the patient might be taking, this is less probable than a G6PD deficiency.

  • While primaquine can have side effects, the rapid onset of jaundice post-medication intake makes an enzyme deficiency a more likely reason.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old sexually active, HIV-negative male visits his healthcare provider with a painless sore on his inner lip and a non-itchy rash on the soles of his feet. He recalls having a non-tender ulcer on his scrotum about a month and a half ago, which resolved on its own. He receives an intramuscular injection of benzathine penicillin G and is discharged. How might the treatment approach for this patient have been modified?

options.label: A
options.text: The choice of antibiotic was not appropriate, and another class should have been selected.

options.label: B
options.text: The correct treatment would involve a different form of penicillin G, rather than benzathine.

options.label: C
options.text: There is no need for changes; the treatment administered is correct.

options.label: D
options.text: After the initial injection, a follow-up dose should be given after 7 days.

questions.answerText: There is no need for changes; the treatment administered is correct.
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. There is no need for changes; the treatment administered is correct.

 

The patient's clinical presentation, including a painless sore followed by a rash on the soles of the feet, is consistent with secondary syphilis.

  • The first-line treatment for syphilis at any stage is penicillin, specifically benzathine penicillin G, which is long-acting and given intramuscularly. Thus, another antibiotic class isn't needed.

  • Benzathine penicillin G is the appropriate form of penicillin for the treatment of syphilis. It is the recommended preparation due to its prolonged action which provides a sustained therapeutic level for an extended period.

  • The single intramuscular injection of benzathine penicillin G is the appropriate treatment for early syphilis, which includes both primary and secondary stages.

  • A single dose of benzathine penicillin G is sufficient for the treatment of primary or secondary syphilis in HIV-negative individuals. The follow-up dose after 7 days is recommended for the late latent stage or tertiary syphilis, but not for early syphilis.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman presents to the clinic with recurrent vaginal itching and discharge. She reports that over-the-counter antifungal creams have provided only temporary relief. Given her history, the physician decides to initiate a prescription antifungal regimen. Based on the mechanisms of action of various antifungal medications, which of the following statements is incorrectly matched?

options.label: D
options.text: Amphotericin B - Create artificial pores in the membrane

questions.solutionHtml:
ring with fungal DNA and RNA synthesis. It is converted to 5-fluorouracil within the fungal cell, which then inhibits thymidylate synthase, thereby disrupting DNA and RNA synthesis.

Explanation of Other Options

A. Azoles - Inhibit ergosterol synthesis

This statement is correct. Azoles inhibit the enzyme lanosterol 14α-demethylase, which is crucial for the synthesis of ergosterol, an essential component of the fungal cell membrane.

C. Echinocandins - Inhibit glycan synthesis

This statement is correct. Echinocandins inhibit the enzyme β-(1,3)-D-glucan synthase, which is essential for the synthesis of β-(1,3)-D-glucan, an important component of the fungal cell wall.

D. Amphotericin B - Create artificial pores in the membrane

This statement is correct. Amphotericin B binds to ergosterol in the fungal cell membrane, creating pores that increase membrane permeability and lead to cell death.

Educational Objective

Understanding the mechanisms of action of antifungal medications is essential for effective treatment. Azoles inhibit ergosterol synthesis, echinocandins inhibit glycan synthesis, and amphotericin B creates artificial pores in the fungal cell membrane. Flucytosine, however, works by interfering with fungal DNA and RNA synthesis, not by inhibiting microtubules.

questions.stem: A 42-year-old man is diagnosed with both HIV and chronic hepatitis B infection. His physician is considering a treatment regimen that can effectively address both conditions. Which of the following antiretroviral medications would also have activity against hepatitis B virus?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A. Lamivudine

 

  • Lamivudine:
    In the context of a patient with both HIV and HBV infections, Lamivudine stands out as a viable choice because it is a nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) that has activity against both viruses. It inhibits the reverse transcriptase enzyme, thereby suppressing viral replication for both HIV and HBV.
  • Indinavir:
    Indinavir is a protease inhibitor used primarily for the treatment of HIV infection. It does not have efficacy against HBV, making it unsuitable for treating both conditions in this patient.
  • Didanosine:
    Didanosine is another NRTI but is mainly used for treating HIV. It is not effective against HBV, so it would not meet the criteria for treating both conditions in this patient.
  • Efavirenz:
    Efavirenz is a non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI) used for HIV treatment. It does not have activity against HBV, making it an inappropriate choice for treating both conditions simultaneously.

questions.stem: Ganciclovir is preferred over acyclovir in the following condition:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Cytomegalovirus retinitis in AIDS patients

 

  • Herpes simplex keratitis:
    Acyclovir is usually the antiviral of choice for treating herpes simplex infections, including keratitis. Ganciclovir is not the first choice for herpes simplex conditions.
  • Cytomegalovirus retinitis in AIDS patients:
    Ganciclovir is specifically effective against cytomegalovirus (CMV) and is the preferred choice for treating CMV retinitis, especially in AIDS patients. Acyclovir is not as effective against CMV.
  • Herpes zoster:
    Acyclovir is typically used for treating herpes zoster (shingles). Ganciclovir is not the first-line treatment for herpes zoster.
  • Chickenpox:
    Acyclovir is also commonly used to treat chickenpox, especially in severe or complicated cases. Ganciclovir is not recommended for chickenpox treatment.


erred choice for treating CMV retinitis, especially in AIDS patients. Acyclovir is not as effective against CMV.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man presents to the emergency room with seizures. A CT scan of his head reveals a space-occupying lesion, suggesting a diagnosis of neurocysticercosis. Which of the following medications is not recommended for treating this patient's condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Di-Ethyl-Carbamezine

 

  • Carbamazepine:
    Carbamazepine is an anticonvulsant medication commonly used to control seizures. Given that the patient presented with seizures, this drug would be an appropriate choice for symptom management.

  • Di-Ethyl-Carbamezine:
    Di-Ethyl-Carbamezine is not typically used for treating neurocysticercosis or seizures associated with it. In fact, it is used for the treatment of filariasis and is not recommended for neurocysticercosis.

  • Albendazole:
    Albendazole is an antiparasitic medication that is commonly used for treating neurocysticercosis. It kills the cysticercus, the larval form of the Taenia solium tapeworm that causes the condition.

  • Prednisolone:
    Prednisolone is a corticosteroid that may be used to reduce inflammation and edema around the cysts in the brain, especially during the initial phase of anthelmintic therapy, to avoid inflammatory responses as the parasites die.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man presents to the clinic with complaints of severe headaches, disturbances in sleep, and intermittent fever for the past few weeks. He recently returned from a trip to Central Africa. Lumbar puncture results reveal trypanosomes in the cerebrospinal fluid, suggesting a late-stage African trypanosomiasis with CNS involvement. Which drug would be most effective in treating both the blood and CNS stages of his condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Melarsoprol

 

  • Emetine:
    Emetine is used primarily to treat amoebic infections and is not effective against trypanosomes, which cause African sleeping sickness.
  • Melarsoprol:
    Melarsoprol is an arsenical compound effective in treating both the blood and CNS stages of African trypanosomiasis. It is the drug of choice for late-stage CNS involvement.
  • Nifurtimox:
    Nifurtimox is another drug used for treating African trypanosomiasis but is generally used in combination with eflornithine for the late-stage disease. It is less effective than melarsoprol for CNS involvement.
  • Suramin:
    Suramin is effective against early stages of African trypanosomiasis and clears the trypanosomes from the blood and lymph nodes. However, it is not effective for late-stage CNS involvement.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman presents to her gynecologist with complaints of vaginal discharge and a fishy odor. After taking a history and performing a pelvic exam, a wet mount preparation shows a "clue cell" pattern. The pH of the vaginal fluid is found to be above 4.5. The diagnosis of bacterial vaginosis is made. Which of the following is the recommended first-line treatment for bacterial vaginosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
administered either orally or intravaginally and is known for its efficacy in treating this condition.

Explanation of Other Options

A. Fluconazole

Fluconazole is an antifungal medication used primarily to treat yeast infections, such as vaginal candidiasis. It is not effective against the bacteria that cause BV.

B. Clindamycin

Clindamycin is another effective treatment for BV and can be used as an alternative to metronidazole. However, it is not the first-line treatment.

D. Ciprofloxacin

Ciprofloxacin is an antibiotic used to treat various bacterial infections, but it is not recommended for the treatment of BV. It is more commonly used for urinary tract infections and certain types of bacterial diarrhea.

Educational Objective

Bacterial vaginosis is commonly treated with metronidazole, which is effective against the anaerobic bacteria associated with the condition. It can be administered orally or intravaginally. Understanding the appropriate treatment options for BV ensures effective management and resolution of symptoms, such as vaginal discharge and odor.
